patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average with a zero-lag double-smoothing filter (DSSA / "zero-lag EMA" style error-correction). A single EMA introduces phase lag proportional to window length, hurting lag_error and responsiveness. The zero-lag technique runs two passes of EMA and adds back the estimated lag error (error = input - EMA of EMA, corrected output = 2*EMA1 - EMA2), which cancels most of the group delay while retaining strong noise attenuation. This simultaneously reduces lag_error (error correction term), slope changes and false reversals (smoother trend), while improving correlation since output tracks the clean signal phase-aligned. To keep output length consistent with the current API, the filter is applied on the full signal and the last output_length values are returned, aligned to the window end as before.
